stem: A newborn nursery audit reviews 200 male infants. Approximately how many would be expected to have cryptorchidism detected at birth?
explanation: Cryptorchidism is expected in about 3 to 5% of male newborns at birth, so in 200 infants this corresponds to roughly 6 to 10 cases.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because 2 to 4 out of 200 is about 1 to 2%, which is below the expected birth incidence.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because 3 to 5% of 200 male infants is approximately 6 to 10 infants.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 20 to 30 out of 200 is about 10 to 15%, which is higher than the expected incidence.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 60 to 90 out of 200 would be 30 to 45%, far above the expected incidence.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because more than 100 out of 200 would mean over 50%, which is not consistent with cryptorchidism at birth.
